title: Noun-based resource surface with scoped hierarchy and declared representations
iWant: every capability expressed as a resource with a predictable URL and one documented representation
soThat: I can discover, cache, and integrate against the surface without reading the server source

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every collection URL is a plural noun; no path segment under the versioned root is a verb or verb phrase.
acceptanceCriteria.when: path segments are checked against the resource model
acceptanceCriteria.then: every segment is a plural noun, a resource identifier, or a declared sub-resource; none is a verb

acceptanceCriteria.description: Nested paths exist only for genuinely 1:N, always-scoped relationships; a resource reachable without its parent is not nested under it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the declared resource model and the path inventory
acceptanceCriteria.when: each nested path is compared against the relationship it models
acceptanceCriteria.then: every nested path corresponds to a declared 1:N always-scoped relationship and no independent resource is parent-scoped

acceptanceCriteria.description: Collection filters are expressed as query parameters or declared sub-resources, never as ad-hoc path segments.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a filtered view of a collection
acceptanceCriteria.then: the filter travels as documented query parameters or a declared sub-resource path, not an invented segment

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every resource class has exactly one documented representation model, and every endpoint returning that class returns that representation.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two different endpoints returning the same resource class
acceptanceCriteria.when: their response bodies are compared field by field
acceptanceCriteria.then: both conform to the same documented representation model

acceptanceCriteria.description: Standard verb semantics hold: GET is safe and cacheable, PUT and DELETE are idempotent, POST creates or triggers, PATCH partially updates; no endpoint repurposes a verb against its semantics.
acceptanceCriteria.when: each operation's verb and behaviour are reviewed
acceptanceCriteria.then: every operation's behaviour matches its verb's declared semantics

acceptanceCriteria.description: Mutating a resource returns the resulting representation (or a Location header on 201) so clients never need a follow-up read to learn the outcome.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a successful POST, PUT, or PATCH
acceptanceCriteria.then: the body carries the resulting representation, or the 201 response carries a Location header resolving to it
